subject: Provisional rate relief request from NobleHealth for delayed routing integration
messages:
From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@noblehealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: Interim pricing request — integration delay impact

Hi Rachel,

Quick note from our side — our engineering team hit an unexpected blocker with the embeddings-only routing change that was expected in the 2027.05 release. The feature was critical for our pipeline because it allows us to route high-volume requests to a cheaper embedding model; without it we've seen token costs spike and latency variance that prevents us from launching the new patient-facing workflow on schedule.

We have the contract and SOW in place (attached usage snapshot for the last 30 days). Can Redwood provide a provisional rate relief (discount or credit) for the period where we can't use the optimized routing? We're not asking for a permanent pricing change — just a temporary accommodation until routing is delivered and we validate it in our staging.

Key asks: 1) provisional discount applied to invoices for the affected weeks, 2) commitment on expected delivery window for the routing fix, 3) acceptance criteria so we can sign off quickly.

We appreciate how quickly the team has been helping — pulling in your legal/finance folks now so this can move fast.

Thanks,
Maria Lopez
Senior Product Manager, Integrations
NobleHealth
Attachment: NobleHealth_usage_snapshot.csv (CSV, 48KB)
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, finance@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Interim pricing request — NobleHealth (needs exec signoff)

Forwarding NobleHealth's note. TL;DR: customer launched a feature that depends on our embeddings routing; they can't go live until the routing path is available. They are asking for a temporary discount/credit. Attachments: usage snapshot and SOW link (Drive).

Proposed commercial response (sales suggested):
- Provisional 20% credit against token usage invoiced during the impacted weeks, retro to 2027-05-01, capped at $40k, applied as a one-time invoice credit.
- Condition: we require product to confirm a commit window and provide acceptance test within 3 weeks; customer must validate routing in staging.

Product notes/questions I need answered before we sign off:
- Karthik: what's the realistic earliest ship date for the routing variant for Noble's workload? Any risk it slips beyond 3 weeks?
- Grace: are there any quick mitigations (config or temporary routing) that would reduce their exposure and maybe reduce the credit amount?

Please reply with approvals, adjustments to the commercial proposal, or objections. If we can get executive signoff from Laura, I'll send a formal commercial offer to Maria and finance to produce the credit.

—Rachel
Rachel Kim
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Fwd: Interim pricing request — NobleHealth (needs exec signoff)

Thanks for flagging — quick technical context: the routing variant depends on a small change to the model catalog selection and a targeted kernel scheduling tweak. The core work is done; the remaining items are QA and a compatibility test for the customer's long-seq embedding calls. I think a conservative delivery window is 10–14 calendar days assuming no new regressions. If we put a small canary (limited percentage) on their account earlier, we can get them most of the benefit within 7 days.

Mitigation options:
- Canary routing (recommended): enable routing for 5–10% of their traffic today — low risk, gives significant cost reduction.
- Temporary token-throttling + cache warming: lowers their ops cost but doesn't fully recover the embedding routing benefit.

Commercial impact: if we can get them the canary in 7 days, I'd support a smaller provisional credit (10–12%) with a one-week retro. If we need to wait the full QA window, the higher 18–20% cap is more defensible. 

Happy to pair with engineering to spin up the canary — cc'ing Marissa for rollout ops.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Product — Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, finance@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 18:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: Interim pricing request — NobleHealth (needs exec signoff)

Thanks team — I've reviewed the ask and the proposed mitigations. Given the customer relationship and the fact this is a product timing issue (not an integration error on their side), I approve a one-time provisional credit. Details below: 

- Approved remedy: apply an 18% credit to token usage invoiced for the period 2027-05-01 through 2027-05-21, capped at $35,000.
- Conditions: engineering will enable a 5% canary routing for Noble within 7 calendar days (Karthik/Marissa to own). Customer must validate routing in staging and confirm by email within 5 business days of canary kick-off. If the canary proceeds successfully, we will not extend or renew the credit beyond the one-time amount.
- Next steps: Rachel, please send a formal commercial confirmation to Maria with the credit terms and the acceptance criteria. Finance, please prepare the invoice credit line item code NH-CREDIT-202705 and confirm the accounting treatment.

This keeps the accommodation bounded while we move quickly to fix the underlying product timeline. Thanks for coordinating.

Laura Bennett
VP, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
